title: Foldr — Team Drive
objective: Alice works in the Campaigns folder of the company drive and has edit rights there. Edit a file in a folder above it — one you were never given edit rights on.

verifier.condition: A file is edited by a user who has no editor grant on its folder or on any ancestor folder, only on a folder below it.

weakness: The effective-role resolver counts grants on descendants as well as ancestors of a folder (a navigation shortcut), and the file-write endpoint reuses it, so an editor grant deep in the tree gives edit rights on every folder above it.
seededData: Folder tree Company > Finance > Payroll and Company > Marketing > Campaigns with synthetic files in each. alice has an editor grant on Campaigns only; tess owns the root. In memory; reset with the instance.
hints: Look at the access label the drive shows for each folder you can see. Not every folder you can open is one you can change.
Permissions are supposed to flow downward from where they were granted. Test whether the server only ever applies them in that direction.
Open a folder above Campaigns, note a file id from its listing, and send an edit for it yourself.
burpNotes: Browse the folders you can see and compare the access label on each with what the API lets you do. The listing shows file ids; the edit button only appears where the interface thinks you may use it.
